Subject: Questions on backup retention, erase propagation and who triggers final deletion

Hi Laura,

We ran through our records and have a couple of items we need clarified before GreenBank signs the updated DPA:

1) If an account-level delete is requested by our admin, how and when does that deletion propagate to backups and cross-region replicas?
2) Who within Redwood has the authority to request a full expunge (beyond soft-delete retention) — can an account admin trigger immediate physical removal via the console or do you require a formal signed request?
3) If Redwood deletes the encryption key for a dataset, is that considered irreversible (i.e., renders encrypted backups unrecoverable)?
4) What evidence/attestation do you provide once an expunge completes (audit record, snapshot ids, timestamps)?

We appreciate a short plain-English summary and a pointer to any templates/procedures so we can map into our legal/ops checklist.

Thanks,

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Sean (security & compliance) to confirm the technical and policy details. We’ve also attached a compact retention matrix and our expunge-request template for your review.

High-level answers up front:
- Standard console deletes initiate a soft-delete path; backups remain subject to configured retention windows and legal holds.
- Formal, account-wide forced expunges require a Redwood-signed attestation workflow (signed request + account owner approval). This cannot be initiated solely from the self-serve console.
- Key destruction in our KMS workflow is treated as rendering data unrecoverable once keys are cryptographically zeroed; we document the key lifecycle and provide attestation of KMS key destruction when used as part of an expunge.

Hi all — technical details below (keeping it non-cryptic):

1) Backup cadence and retention
- Live snapshots: incremental snapshots every 4 hours, full snapshot daily.
- Primary snapshot retention (default for most accounts): 45 days.
- Cross-region replicated snapshots: copied asynchronously and retained for 180 days by default for replicated copies; we can extend to 365 days for enterprise plans.

2) Delete flow and propagation
- A console-initiated account delete transitions records to a soft-delete state immediately. That triggers a tombstone marker that prevents further serving reads and schedules the object for expunge per retention policy.
- Tombstone propagation to replica metadata occurs within 0–96 hours depending on in-flight replication; actual physical expunge (where snapshot blocks get reclaimed) is batched and executed in waves to avoid disrupting active replication — typical full expunge across all copies can take up to 45 days from the initial delete, depending on retention windows and region replication queues.

3) KMS / key destruction
- Our KMS policy requires a three-step key retirement (disable -> scheduled destruction -> zeroization). Once a key is zeroized and destroyed it is cryptographically irrecoverable. We provide the key id and destruction timestamp as part of the expunge attestation. Note: key destruction is an irreversible step and we treat requests that include key destruction as final.

4) Legal hold & exceptions
- Legal holds block expunge and override retention schedules until released. Holds are sticky and require the issuing party (GreenBank legal contact) to request release through the attestation workflow.

5) Evidence / audit trail
- We keep an immutable audit trail for delete/expunge operations (requester id, timestamps, snapshot ids, affected object ids, region copies) and can provide a signed attestation PDF and a CSV export of the log entries on completion.

If you need a narrower SLA for expunge completion (e.g., accelerate replication sweep), we can discuss a dedicated runbook / committed window as part of an enterprise addendum.

—Karthik

Michael — quick answers to your follow-ups: 

• Upper bound for DPA: we recommend documenting a conservative upper bound of 60 days for cross-region expunge completion in the DPA (this covers queued replications, legal hold reconciliations, and admin windows). In standard cases the sweep completes in ~30 days; 60 days is our contractual cap for the expunge run for accounts on enterprise plans.

• Attestation & authorization: we require a signed expunge request (DocuSign) from the account owner plus an internal approval from Redwood Security (role: Head of Security Operations or their delegate). We’ll accept a standing account-level authorization on file if you prefer (one signed master authorization covers future expunges), but we still require the expunge request to be initiated via the attestation workflow (link below).

• Redwood approver: Head of Security Operations (currently Sean Gallagher) will be the approver role recorded in your matrix; the redwood signatory on the attestation will be a delegated Security Operations lead and the Compliance team will issue the final signed attestation document once the expunge completes.

I’ve attached our expunge template and the retention matrix. If you want, I can draft a one-paragraph DPA clause wording you can drop into your internal checklist.

Laura
